kill_argument: The result is close to predictable before any outcome is read. The notes give published estimates on this sample from related estimators: AIPW-GRF $1,571 (SE 704), entropy balancing $1,406 (655). The placebo is expected to fail (Imbens-Xu), and runtime shows it may be unable to pass at all, since a pass needs SE_p < 459. The NSW 're74' period mismatch also means neither placebo verdict isolates confounding. So the likely paper is 'positive contrast, placebo failed, reported as a statistical contrast', and its contribution is procedural only. All of this is disclosed in plan.json contribution, hypotheses and threats, and accepted at the question gate, so it does not block the design. What I attacked that held: the restored components match the adopted design at 716b6c3 except for the listed mechanical changes; the pre-diagnostic plan is proven (hash 320cc2 rebuilt, diff = diagnostics and one task status only); question, hypotheses and constraints are unchanged since the question gate; nothing is fitted under X- with the real treatment; RE78 is never parsed; the run records now name the right interpreter with identical diagnostics; and no file compares an estimate with the benchmark. The remaining objection: rob-covsets (a) omits race (F6).

findings.text: DEV-9 and DEV-11 remove, at the design stage and with the literature in view, the adopted robustness and sensitivity components that the crew's notes predict would weaken the headline. The reason DEV-9 gives is wrong for four of them. (1) sens-imbens: the adopted identifying_assumption (ss-null-effect plan.json design.method.identifying_assumption, commit 716b6c3) says 'The assumption is probed only by sens-imbens ... and by rob-diff74'. Here both are dropped, and threats[0] concedes the assumption is 'untested beyond H3', a placebo the crew expects to fail and calls possibly uninformative. (2) rob-covsets: the adopted design lists it as a trigger in its disagreement rule. Covariate-set sensitivity is the best-documented fragility on LDW-CPS: sources/notes.md sec. 2 on smith2005, and DW 1999 Sec. 5.2, where dropping RE74 moves the CPS estimates to $861-$1,941. rob-covsets (b), 'all covariates except re74 and u74', is that exact check. (3) rob-estimators: notes.md sec. 2 records regression 1,066 (554) and IPW 1,236.84 (687.14) on this sample. Both CIs include zero, so the reported robustness table would show the H1 decision differing by estimator. Advani et al. (notes.md sec. 3) advise reporting a range of estimators, and the Scout's own implication says the paper should report a small set of secondary estimators. (4) rob-diff74: smith2005 find DID matching performs best on this benchmark. None of these 'answers a hypothesis this question does not have'. Each is a check on H1 or its assumption. The track playbook (crew/tracks/social-science.md) asks for 'checks that could fail' and robustness 'including those that weaken the result'. The cuts are disclosed (DEV-9; threats[0]), but under a reason that hides what they do. Runtime is not a constraint: design.runtime projects 4.4 of 30 minutes.

findings.text: For NSW men, re74 is not 1974 earnings, and both the identifying assumption and the H3 placebo assume it is. smith2005 (Sec. 5, pp. 322-323, in the Scout's fetched text) states that DW's 'Re74' for NSW men is 'real earnings in months 13-24 prior to the month of random assignment ... For persons randomly assigned later in the experiment, these months largely overlap with 1975'. For CPS men it is calendar-1974 SSA earnings. Smith-Todd also reconstruct DW's sample rule: everyone randomly assigned in January-April 1976, but men assigned after April 1976 only if their 'Re74' is zero. So for a share of the 185 treated, u74 = 1 by sample construction, measured over months that overlap 1975. Consequences. (a) Main design: X contains a covariate measured over different periods in the two groups, which is a direct threat to unconfoundedness given X. design.threats lists survey-versus-SSA measurement but not this. (b) H3: placebo-re75 takes calendar-1975 earnings as its outcome and conditions on re74 and u74. For later-assigned treated men, that covariate spans much of the same months and was used to select them into the sample. The placebo contrast therefore mixes selection on the 1975 shock with a definitional and sample-selection link between X- and the outcome that exists only for treated men. This is a second reason, beyond the Ashenfelter dip the plan names, why a fail does not show bias. It also means a pass, which licenses 'effect' wording under hypotheses[0], could arise mechanically. data/CODEBOOK.md defines re74 as 'earnings in 1974' for all units.

findings.text: rob-trim cannot do much of what the plan says it tests. method.control_only_trimming and analysis_plan say it measures 'dependence on CPS men outside the treated propensity range'. In an AIPW ATT, those men enter the estimate only through their weight m/(1-m) and through the nuisance fits. From runs/diag-overlap/propensity.csv, the 8,125 CPS men rob-trim drops carry 0.169 of the 188.9 total m_bar-weight, or 0.09%. I computed this arithmetic on the existing outcome-free diag-overlap output; no model was fitted and no outcome was read. So rob-trim tests only whether re-fitting g0 and m on the 7,867 kept men moves the estimate. The trim count also hinges on one treated man: the cutoff is the single lowest treated m_bar (1.03e-4). At the second- or third-lowest treated value, 9,218 or 11,193 CPS men would be dropped. Because rob-trim is one of the three checks in the disagreement rule (threats[11]), the rule rests in practice on rob-learners.

findings.text: The mechanical DEV-13 mapping turns rob-covsets (a), a trigger of the disagreement rule, into a check that omits race. The adopted rule keeps age, educ, married and the earnings history and drops the rest. On the synthetic file the dropped covariates were urban, region, children and health_limit. Here the same rule drops black, hisp and nodegree. black is by far the most imbalanced covariate in this sample: its raw normalized difference is 1.72 (runs/diag-overlap/metrics.json nd_raw_black), larger than re74 (-1.11) or re75 (-1.23). So under (a) the comparison is no longer the covariate-set sensitivity the adopted design cites (Smith-Todd's specifications all include race). It is unconfoundedness without race, an assumption the design's own identifying_assumption rejects. The direction of the resulting bias is foreseeable. Treated men are mostly black, and black CPS men earn less, so omitting race likely raises the imputed counterfactual and lowers the estimate. That pushes (a) toward a decision difference, and threats[14] would then make the abstract say the conclusion 'is not robust to that check'. The rule is conservative, not a search toward a favourable result. But as worded, the abstract would describe an omitted-confounder result as covariate-set fragility. nodegree is nearly redundant given educ and educ^2, so dropping it matters little.
